content: CQRS / materialized-read-model separation is the standard pattern when read and write shapes differ and read:write traffic is highly asymmetric (public analytics-style dashboard reads far outnumbering admin writes) -- explicitly named as a canonical CQRS use case in Microsoft's Azure Architecture Center. Lightweight CQRS with a shared underlying database (write side updates canonical tables; a view/materialized view/background refresh job produces the denormalized read model) is recommended over full event-sourced CQRS unless independent scaling of reads/writes is required. This validates a public read-only map (denormalized/cached segment view) separated from an authority read/write dashboard (operates on canonical entities) without needing full CQRS/event sourcing machinery.
